verdicts.evidence: Symbolic simplification to zero for N=3–6 and numeric tests across 240 configs show float64 drift of 4.4e-16 and float32 drift of 7.4e-8, matching the paper's reported band; mutation tests (asymmetric inflow, non-periodic BC) produce drift ≥1e5× larger, confirming the shared-flux/periodic mechanism.

Symbolic worst-case margins are strictly positive (a(1−α)>0, b(1−β)>0); numeric tests across 540 configs including adversarial logit scale 20 and cells starting on-bound show 0/540 violations with worst excursion <4e-15; mutation test replacing σ with 1.6σ yields 120/120 violations, attributing the guarantee to the capacity fraction.

No code or dataset was released, no trained model was produced, and no toy substitute was attempted; the MAE numbers (3.12e-3 vs 6.74e-3) are entirely untested, and the logbook notes the comparison crosses backbone categories.

Same data/training blockers as Claim 3 prevent any reproduction of the MAE or violation-rate numbers; the logbook additionally records that the quoted 1.87% upper-bound violation rate matches neither printed table value (2.87% ResNet, 2.01% FNO).

The 17.3× speedup is defined relative to a GPU solver and no GPU was available; three trained FluxNet-D models on unreleased Cahn–Hilliard trajectories are required, and no toy substitute or partial timing was produced.

With untrained independent branch logits, 6/6 seeds show bound violations (mean 3.27% lb, 2.65% ub), confirming no architectural guarantee; minimizing L_DCL on logits drives violations to 0.00% on 6/6 seeds (L_DCL 0.195→1.04e-8); sign-flip mutation causes violations to persist and grow, and Spearman ρ=0.903 (p=4.8e-34) links DCL residual to violation magnitude.

overall: The logbook rigorously verifies the paper's mathematical propositions (conservation, L/U-head bounds, DCL-as-enforcer) through 240–540-config numeric sweeps plus mutation tests on a faithful from-the-paper numpy implementation. All trained-model accuracy and speedup claims (Tables 3–5) remain inconclusive due to unreleased data, no code, and no GPU, with no toy substitutes attempted.
